glance: Home kitchens and some sweet shops in Lalmonirhat and Hatibandha
kaun-payesh.desc: Kaun (foxtail millet) grows well on the sandy chars and dry lands of the Teesta, where rice is hard to raise. Cooked slowly with milk, sugar or gur and a bay leaf, it becomes a soft, nutty payesh. It was once an everyday grain for river families and is now enjoyed as a treat. Its small, round grains give it a texture different from rice pudding.
blocks: Good to know
Look for kaun grain in local markets if you want to cook it yourself.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
kakina-zamindar-bari.desc: Kakina, in Kaliganj upazila, was the seat of one of the notable zamindar families of the region. Parts of the old estate, including gateways and buildings, survive among later houses and trees. Locally it is linked with the zamindar Mahima Ranjan Roy Chowdhury, remembered for his interest in culture and learning. It is a quiet glimpse of the cultural life of the old north.
blocks: How to get there
Kakina is on the Lalmonirhat–Patgram road; take a bus to Kakina bazar and ask locally.
Good to know
Parts are private homes now; ask before entering.

tin-bigha-corridor.desc: Dahagram and Angarpota form a piece of Bangladesh surrounded by India, linked to the mainland by the Tin Bigha Corridor, a strip of land only a few hundred metres long. For years it opened only at set hours, but since 2011 the corridor has been open around the clock for Bangladeshis. Crossing it and seeing the villages of Dahagram beside the Teesta is a vivid lesson in the region's tangled border history. The surrounding landscape is rural and calm.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or train to Patgram upazila, then an auto-rickshaw to the corridor.
Good to know
Carry national ID or passport. Photography of border installations may be restricted; follow guards' instructions.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
teesta-rail-and-road-bridges.desc: Here the Teesta is crossed by an old railway bridge and, beside it, a road bridge opened in 2012. The rail bridge, with Lalmonirhat Sadar on its north end and Kaunia upazila of Rangpur on its south, also carried road traffic from 1978 until the new bridge took over. Today trains still rumble across it while buses use its neighbour. In the dry season the river splits into channels between wide sandbanks, and in the monsoon it runs broad and fast. Local people gather on the banks in the evening to watch the sun go down over the water.
blocks: How to get there
From Lalmonirhat town take a bus, CNG or auto south towards Teesta/Kaunia; from Rangpur, buses to Lalmonirhat cross the road bridge.
Good to know
Never walk on the railway bridge. Watch from the banks or the road bridge's walkway, and take care with traffic.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
tushbhandar-zamindar-bari.desc: Tushbhandar was the seat of another zamindar family of the region, and their old residence still stands in Kaliganj upazila. Brick walls with arched openings, decorative details and family temples remain, weathered by time. There is no formal visitor setup, so a visit feels like stepping into a forgotten corner. Local people are usually happy to point the way.
blocks: How to get there
From Lalmonirhat take a bus to Kaliganj, then an auto-rickshaw to Tushbhandar.
Good to know
Respect temples that are still in use and avoid unstable structures.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
noudabas-sal-forest.desc: Noudabas Shalban is a sal forest of roughly 83 hectares in Noudabas union of Hatibandha upazila, about 6 km east of the upazila town. Locals reckon the forest is around two hundred years old. Under the old sal trees the Forest Department has planted cane, and foxes, jungle cats, mongooses and monitor lizards live here. In winter migratory birds add to the resident species. It sees almost no tourists, which is exactly its charm.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Lalmonirhat to Hatibandha (about 60 km), then an auto or van about 6 km east to Noudabas.
Good to know
Go in daylight and in company; there are no facilities. Ask the forest beat office or villagers about paths.

glance: Home-style eateries in Lalmonirhat town, or with a local family
lalmonirhat-pelka.desc: Pelka is a traditional dish of the Rangpur region made by cooking leafy greens, often jute leaves, with a pinch of soda until they turn smooth and slippery. It is lightly spiced and sometimes enriched with small fish or dried fish. Families serve it with plain rice, especially in the lean seasons, and for many it tastes of home. Ask a local family or a home-style eatery to try it.
blocks: Good to know
It is mild and soothing; pair it with a spicy bhorta.

glance: About 260–600 BDT per kg depending on the sweet
Pradip Mistanna Bhandar, Goshala Bazar, Lalmonirhat town
lalmonirhat-pradip-sweets.desc: Subal Chandra Saha founded Pradip Mistanna Bhandar in 1967, and it has been the town's trusted name for sweets ever since. The counter holds rasgolla, chomchom, rasmalai, kalojam, lalmohan, pantua, rajbhog, khirmohon, doi and several kinds of sandesh. Visitors and Lalmonirhat people living abroad take boxes home from here. Prices sit at the ordinary end for a famous shop.

glance: winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), late autumn (Oct–Nov) and autumn (Aug–Sep)
burimari-land-port.desc: Burimari, at the northern tip of Patgram upazila, faces Changrabandha in India. Trucks carrying stones, fruit and goods queue on the road, and travellers cross on foot towards Siliguri, Darjeeling, Sikkim and Bhutan. The small town around the port has a frontier feel, with money changers and eateries. Even if you are not crossing, it is interesting to watch the traffic of people and trade.
blocks: How to get there
Direct buses run from Dhaka and Rangpur to Burimari; trains reach Burimari station as well.
Good to know
You need a valid passport and visa to cross. Arrive early to avoid long queues.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
lalmonirhat-railway-heritage.desc: Lalmonirhat grew up as a railway junction in the British era and became the headquarters of one of the country's railway divisions. Old brick offices, staff quarters, a railway hospital and wide roads lined with trees still define the town centre. Railway jobs shaped its community, and many families can trace their roots to the trains. Walking around the station area shows a slower, older side of North Bengal.
blocks: How to get there
Lalmonirhat station is in the town centre; trains run from Dhaka and Rangpur.
Good to know
Some railway premises are restricted; enjoy the public areas and streets.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
sindurmati-dighi.desc: Sindurmati Tirthadham grew up around an old dighi in Sindurmati mouza, on the border of Lalmonirhat and Kurigram districts. Legend says a zamindar named Raj Narayan Chakraborty dug it hoping for children, and named it after his daughters Sindur and Moti. On Ram Navami in the month of Chaitra a big fair is held, and pilgrims from far away take a holy dip in the tank. When the dighi was re-excavated in 1975, old coins and images were found, now kept in the National Museum. Outside fair days it is a quiet, tree-lined place.
blocks: How to get there
From Lalmonirhat town take an auto or CNG south-east towards the Kurigram border; ask for Sindurmati.
Good to know
Visit at Ram Navami (Chaitra, around March–April) for the fair, but expect big crowds. Respect bathing pilgrims' privacy when taking photos.

glance: 355 km to Lalmonirhat by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
harano-masjid-ramdas.desc: In Ramdas mouza of Panchagram union, a patch of jungle locals called 'Masjider Ara' hid the brick foundations of a small mosque, uncovered when the land was cleared in the 1980s. A small stone inscription found in the ruins carries the kalima and the date 69 Hijri (about 688–689 AD), and it is now kept at the Tajhat Palace museum in Rangpur. If correct, it would make this one of the oldest mosques in South Asia, but historians treat the claim with caution. Only the low foundations of a building about 21 feet wide remain, beside a newer mosque named for the Companions of the Prophet. Visitors come mostly for the story.
blocks: How to get there
From Lalmonirhat town take an auto towards the Rangpur–Kurigram highway; the site is about 1 km south of it in Ramdas, Panchagram union.
Good to know
Dress modestly as it is next to an active mosque. Sindurmati Dighi is a short ride away.
